text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Unemployment rises in July to rate of 11.4 percent.
- Statistics show population in Germany tops 82 million for first time.
- Government wants to sell its stake in DSL Bank to Deutsche Postbank AG.
- Education Minister Juergen Ruettgers says situation in apprenticeship market is somewhat improved.
HANDELSBLATT
- Divergence between east and west German labour market becomes ever greater.
- Ruling coalition plans to use income from reform of pensions system to help finance cut in "solidarity surcharge" on income tax.
- Economic institutes say prospects for east German businesses have improved but economic situation is still far from producing a self-sustaining upturn.
- Building trade desribes failure of government's tax reform plans as "catastrophic".
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Premier of Saxony-Anhalt state describes plans to cut "solidarity surcharge" on income tax as a catastrophe.
- Hans-Olaf Henkel, head of Confederation of German Industry, calls for immediate package to reduce tax burden on businesses.
- Germans spending more than ever on their free time, survey by Citibank shows.
- Government sees no need to intervene to check rise of the dollar against the deutschemark.
DIE WELT
- Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, sees chances of compromise in second mediation process over tax reform.
- Liberal Free Democrats (FDP) to ask members this autumn about the future of conscription.
- Water levels on swollen River Oder recede slowly.
